title: serializer binding record
description: One immutable record binding a named artifact schema to a versioned serializer contract, prospective from an explicit commit boundary. Owner-neutral: any producer, any binding subject; it names no company and privileges no party. The serializer contract remains the authority; this record is evidence that a specific forward producer actually implements it, effective from an exact commit. It does NOT migrate historical artifacts. Every reference resolves to an immutable pre-image (repository+revision+path+sha256): a digest alone does not identify what it is the digest of.

source_ref.description: An immutable, pre-image-identifying coordinate. repository+revision+path LOCATE the exact bytes; sha256 PINS them. A bare digest is not accepted anywhere in this record, because a hash does not name its own pre-image and cannot be resolved without one.

repository.description: Host-qualified repository, e.g. 'github.com/OWNER/REPO'. A bare SHA is not self-resolving across repositories, so the namespace is machine-explicit.

revision.description: The exact immutable revision (full 40-hex commit) at which the path resolves.

path.description: Path to the bytes within the repository at that revision.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of those exact bytes. Must be reproducible from repository+revision+path.

binding_subject.description: The exact schema/artifact identity being bound, e.g. 'tsei.frozen-artifact'. Not a repo or a producer — the subject of the binding.

serializer_contract.description: The versioned serializer contract this record binds to, resolved to its immutable pre-images. The contract remains the authority; this record is only evidence that a forward producer implements it.

id.description: The versioned serializer contract id, e.g. 'encode-json-utf8-lf.v0'. The version suffix is part of identity; the unversioned name never resolves here.

spec.description: The serializer specification, located and pinned. Replaces a bare spec digest: the digest now travels with the coordinates that resolve to it.

vectors.description: The serializer conformance-vectors, located and pinned. The producer's qualification is measured against THIS exact pre-image.

effective_commit.description: Explicit producer-adoption boundary — not derived implicitly from PR or landing time. This names a commit, not a file, so it carries no path/sha256. An artifact of binding_subject produced AT OR AFTER this commit is bound to serializer_contract.id; everything before it remains historically unversioned. This is the PRODUCER's adoption commit — a conformant encoder merely being available in the contract repo is not evidence the producer adopted it.

repository.description: The producer repository the commit belongs to, host-qualified, e.g. 'github.com/OWNER/REPO'.

commit.description: The exact adoption commit SHA in that repository.

producer_conformance.description: Evidence that the FORWARD producer actually implements the serializer contract.

implementation.description: The genuinely-conformant producer, resolved to immutable source — not a descriptive string. It is the encoder adopted at effective_commit that actually implements the contract for all admitted inputs, NOT a byte-coincidental predecessor that merely reproduced historical bytes.

qualification.description: The conformance evidence qualifying that implementation — structurally resolvable, not a free-form claim. Byte-reproduction of historical artifacts under the new producer is MIGRATION evidence (that the boundary is backward-identical), not conformance evidence for the implementation.

method.description: The only method this schema admits: the implementation passes the contract's pinned conformance vectors. A closed value, so a validator verifies it rather than parsing prose.

vectors.description: The EXACT vectors pre-image the implementation was run against. It MUST be the same pre-image as serializer_contract.vectors — an implementation that passed some other vector set has not been qualified against THIS contract. (Cross-field identity is enforced by the validator, which JSON Schema alone cannot express.)

vector_count.description: How many vectors the implementation passed. A count of zero is not evidence.

non_retroactivity.description: Machine-checkable non-retroactivity semantics — declared, not left to prose.

prospective_only.description: This binding governs only artifacts produced at or after effective_commit.

byte_reproduction_is_not_binding.description: That a historical artifact re-encodes byte-identically under the new producer does NOT make it a serializer_contract.id artifact.

historical_binding_requires_separate_rec.description: Binding a historical identity to the contract, if ever chosen deliberately, requires its own separate immutable legacy-resolution record scoped to that exact historical identity.
